author: @SlawomirNowaczyk

evidence.api_compatibility: No API changes whatsoever. The only touched files are src/cpp/server/routing_policy.cpp (comment only, within class LlmClassifier::build_context_payload) and test/cpp/test_routing_policy_llm_router.cpp (test function rename). No schema, protocol, CLI contract, exported API, or documented behavior was altered.
evidence.documentation: The inline comment in build_context_payload() was improved for accuracy, clarifying that the expose_request_features_ guard applies specifically to the policy parser path (the routing.router sugar's synthesized classifier) rather than implying a general policy-driven decision. No external documentation (guides, API docs, release notes) required updating since there is no user-visible change.
evidence.manual_release_testing: No user-visible surface changed. This PR only rewords an internal code comment and renames a test function — there is no API, CLI flag, GUI element, config option, or installed behavior to exercise. Manual release testing is not applicable.
evidence.post_approval_commits: After @fl0rianr's first approval, the author pushed commit 6b7383ba implementing @fl0rianr's suggested fix (adding the parser-path qualifier and renaming the test), then rebased onto main (45c2bcd9) before @Bekhouche's second approval. These post-approval commits were purely in response to review feedback and did not introduce new behavior, weaken tests, or change the risk profile.
evidence.review: PR #3444 received two approvals. @fl0rianr (smart router specialist per contribute.md) submitted a substantive review at commit 1876b2fa, noting the new comment wording was slightly more absolute than the API guarantees and suggesting qualification with "when constructed through the policy parser" plus a test rename. The author implemented these suggestions in post-approval commit 6b7383ba ("Improved as requested"), which stayed within the spirit and scope of the approved PR before rebase. @Bekhouche then approved the rebased branch (45c2bcd9) with LGTM. Both reviewers have subject matter expertise in smart router areas. The review followed project philosophy: the changes improved code clarity without introducing behavior, aligning with the tenet that user-facing code quality matters.
evidence.security: No security concerns. The changes are a comment reword and test rename with zero behavioral impact. No credentials, network calls, auth changes, permissions, telemetry, or supply-chain changes are involved.
evidence.tests: The test `test_parsed_author_classifier_never_serializes_request_features` in test/cpp/test_routing_policy_llm_router.cpp was renamed from `test_feature_serialization_opt_in`; no test logic was altered. All CI tests passed including C++ unit tests, CodeQL analysis, and the full build-and-release pipeline. No tests were weakened, deleted, or skipped.
